ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached structure shows isoleucine with a COO− group above the alpha carbon. The alpha carbon is bonded to NH3+ on the left, H on the right, and a side chain below. In the side chain, the next carbon is bonded to H on the left, CH3 on the right, CH2CH3 below, and the alpha carbon above. Reasoning: The alpha carbon has four different substituents: COO−, NH3+, H, and the side chain, so it is a stereocenter. The side-chain carbon also has four different substituents: H, CH3, CH2CH3, and the rest of the molecule through the alpha carbon, so it is another stereocenter. With 2 stereocenters and no meso symmetry, the number of optical isomers is 2^2 = 4.

planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to know the requested quantity is the number of optical isomers of isoleucine, not just the naturally occurring biological stereoisomer.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the stereochemistry rule that a molecule with n independent chiral centers has up to 2^n optical isomers, reduced only if symmetry/meso forms are present. Isoleucine has no internal plane of symmetry because the substituent sets around the two stereocenters are not symmetrically equivalent.
